subject: Proposal: SOC 2 re-attestation, audit-log retention amendment & capacity uplift for renewal
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@peregrinehealth.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 12 Sep 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal: SOC 2 re-attestation + retention/capacity request

Hi Jordan —

Quick follow on your upcoming renewal (contract DL-4821). Thank you for the heads-up on Peregrine’s internal timeline — appreciated. Two items surfaced on our side that I want to align on before we lock CLM/DocuSign:

1) SOC 2 re-attestation: we need to provide a customer-facing re-attestation package for your procurement team. If you have an internal SOC2 submission window, please share dates.

2) Audit log retention & capacity: you mentioned longer retention for audit logs (5 years) in last call. Our standard offering today is 2 years for audit logs; we can extend to 3–5 years via an amendment that also includes storage and ingestion capacity adjustments. That typically affects both price and the dedicated pool sizing if you move to reserved capacity.

Ask: can you confirm (a) target retention window, (b) whether you want a Dedicated pool increase (concurrent sessions / reserved GPU hours) vs. burst requests, and (c) whether procurement needs the formal re-attestation package by EOW (Sep 17)?

I’ve looped in Neha (security) and Tessa (solutions) to scope evidence and sizing. I can produce a mutual action plan and a DocuSign amendment once we agree on retention and capacity.

Best,
Jonas Weber

Jonas — thanks for the clear note. A few quick answers:

• Retention: Our security team prefers 5 years for audit logs because of regulatory requirements for our clinical integrations. If there’s a meaningful cost delta, we can discuss a middle ground.
• Capacity: We expect a 40% increase in nightly batch indexing and an uptick in peak inference during business hours — likely need more reserved capacity rather than burst to avoid throttling.
• Timeline: Procurement is aiming to get contract language finalized by Sep 24; we would like the re-attestation package by next Friday (Sep 17) if possible.

I’ve attached our most recent SOC 2 checklist and a sample request form (see attachments). Also cc’ing procurement for formal RFP items.

Jordan Lee

Jonas / team —

Quick compliance plan and evidence list for Peregrine’s procurement:

Proposed evidence bundle (customer-facing):
- SOC 2 Type II PDF (summary cover + control narratives) — public redacted copy (soc2_report_2027.pdf)
- Configuration snapshot & retention policy excerpt — shows retention TTL settings and export paths
- Audit-log sample (first 7 days) with redaction guidance (audit-log-sample.csv)
- Logging architecture diagram + storage lifecycle policy (S3 lifecycle to Glacier)
- Attestation letter confirming data handling and support for extended retention windows

Retention feasibility:
- We can support 5-year retention, but cost increases come from storage + retrieval SLAs and longer-term index retention. For Dedicated customers we can tier logs to cold storage automatically; retrieval times may be slower unless they opt for hot retention at incremental cost.
- Recommend compromise: 3-year hot retention + 2-year cold archive (retrieval within 24 hours). That satisfies most regulatory needs while minimizing hot-storage costs.

Evidence timeline: I can assemble the bundle by EOD Sep 15 if we get confirmation on retention window today. I’ll coordinate with our SOC auditor for the attestation letter; they typically need 48–72 hours to sign off on a customer attestation request.

Questions for Tessa: what is the incremental monthly cost for 5-year (all-hot) vs. 3yr hot / 2yr cold? Also need the capacity SKU for the reserved GPU hours to include in the amendment.

-Neha

Team — numbers below (ballpark for initial AMP):

Capacity sizing options (to cover +40% peak/ingest):
- Option A (Reserved Dedicated Pool): add 2 x p4d-reserved nodes (baseline throughput + smoothing). SKU: DED-P4D-2. Estimated incremental commit: $18,500/month.
- Option B (Reserved + Burst): add 1 x p4d-reserved + burst credits (recommended for first 3 months to validate). SKU: DED-P4D-1 + BURST-100K. Estimated: $11,200/month + burst credits usage.

Audit log retention pricing (monthly incremental):
- 5-year all-hot: ~$7,800/month (hot storage + indexing retention)
- 3yr hot + 2yr cold: ~$3,300/month (cold retrieval SLA 24 hrs)

Recommended path: Option B + 3yr hot / 2yr cold. This keeps near-term costs reasonable and gives us time to instrument lifecycle policies. I’ve attached a pricing sheet with line items (capacity-pricing-sheet.xlsx).

I’ll prepare the amendment language for the capacity SKU and retention tiers — can Laura and Neha confirm the legal/compliance phrasing we should use for the retention SLO?

Thanks,
Tessa Morgan
